method_note: Read the whole target file (2018 lines; the sources block from line 1516 onward was scanned by grep and partial reads). Picked 32 high-risk claims: W3C status/dates of eight drafts and Recommendations, repository licence/archived/push/release metadata via read-only gh api, version strings of PyLD, pySHACL, rdflib, jsonld.js, ESMF, DCAT-AP, ISAITB, the PyLD default canonicalization algorithm (read from the v3.3.0 tag source), the Titanium number conversion (main source), the GS1 Web Vocabulary 1.16 file, JSON-LD API mechanisms (303 exclusion, Link header, 10^21 threshold), SHACL entailment failure rule, Commission Implementing Regulation 2026/1778 articles (read from a PDF copy fetched from afec.es, which is a secondary host of the OJ text), literature DOIs via Crossref/OpenAlex, and the engine mapping claims against src/dppce/adapters. EUR-Lex returned empty content to WebFetch for 2024/1781 and 2023/1542, so those article citations stay not_confirmed. No protected standard was opened. No live DPP system was contacted.

checked.claim: A context Link header (rel http://www.w3.org/ns/json-ld#context) is ignored for application/ld+json and HTML; more than one such header gives 'multiple context link headers'; documentUrl follows redirects except 303; alternate Link with type application/ld+json is followed.
checked.evidence: The API text says the Link header is ignored for application/ld+json, text/html, application/xhtml+xml; several context Link headers reject with 'multiple context link headers'; documentUrl excludes 303 redirects; alternate Link rule present. checked.claim: In RDF conversion a native number with a fraction, or magnitude 10^21 or more, becomes xsd:double in canonical form; integers become xsd:integer.
checked.evidence: Object to RDF conversion applies canonical double form to non-integral numbers and to absolute values of at least 10^21; integers below that threshold use the integer form.

checked.claim: A JSON key with no IRI mapping yields no triple and no error (expansion step not read by the target author).
checked.evidence: Syntax spec states that terms not mapped to an IRI are ignored in RDF-relevant processing. The target author hedged correctly; this closes the gap.

checked.claim: SHACL does not require entailment; a processor that does not support an sh:entailment regime named in the shapes must signal failure.
checked.evidence: Implementations MAY support entailment; if the shapes graph has sh:entailment E and E is unsupported, the processor MUST signal a failure.

missed_items.topic: GS1 resolver linkType behaviour changed from Digital Link 1.1
missed_items.fact: In GS1-Conformant Resolver 1.2.1, a request with linkType=<type> for a type that does not exist gives 404 (possibly with the linkset), whereas GS1 Digital Link 1.1 redirected to the default link. A passport tester using gs1:dpp must expect 404 for an absent link type. The target describes the redirect but not the 404.

missed_items.topic: Proof of registration availability and seal
missed_items.fact: Regulation 2026/1778 Art. 9(3) says the proof of registration is guaranteed by a qualified electronic seal (Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, Art. 38) with a Commission time stamp, and Art. 9(4) keeps it available 90 calendar days. This ties L08 to the engine capabilities evidence.qualified_seal and evidence.rfc3161. Art. 10(3) sets automatic deletion of registration data 10 years after registration unless Union law sets another period.

Art. 8(1)-(5) require registration at model, batch or item level, with batch and model identifiers linked to an item-level passport where they exist; Art. 3(b) provides an API. This matters for identifier checks that the target treats only through L01.

Art. 12(5)-(7) require a search service, publicly documented APIs with machine-readable semantic assets, and free access. A pinned snapshot for data.repository_model could be fetched through these APIs once published.

The textiles ontology repository is CIRPASS-2/ontologie-textiles (not ontologies-textiles); the org also has documentation-battery, dpp-renderer-be, dpp-renderer-fe, dpp-data-extractor and mock-eu-registry, the last of which is a possible comparison fixture for registry.mock.

The CIRPASS-2 docs list battery modules Performance 0.3.0, Materials 0.3.0, Labeling 0.2.1, Categories/Chemistries/Statuses 0.1.1, Extinguisher Classes 0.1.1, Locations and Metals 0.1.0; textile ontology 1.1.2 with 14 pages; all marked draft or not official.
hex-core-service latest GitHub release is v0.0.9 and the product-profile model release is v0.2.0 (2026-08-31); licence NOASSERTION on hex-core-service.

overall: The file is reliable on the points checked. All but two of the 32 re-checked claims on W3C statuses and dates, repository licences, archived flags, push and release dates, versions, the PyLD and Titanium behaviours, JSON-LD API mechanisms, the GS1 vocabulary contents, the Regulation 2026/1778 article numbers, the engine mapping, and the literature metadata matched the primary sources. Two small precision issues: the TopBraid row gives a release date in a field used elsewhere for push dates (the repo was pushed 2026-06-30), and the textiles repository name is ontologie-textiles. The ESPR and Battery Regulation point letters (Art. 10(1)(d), 11(a),(d), 77(5), 78(a)) and the UNTP 'only version' statement could not be independently re-read in this session, so they stay not_confirmed without any sign of error. No rule 5 problem was found: IEC 61360 and the ECLASS IRDI scheme appear as bibliographic or licence metadata only, and the DIN SPEC is mentioned as a reference without content.
